summary: Thin day: Reddit, X and Bluesky were blocked from this environment and search was weak, so only Hacker News yielded verifiable evidence. Two themes had 2+ independent sources: people asking for a standard way to share the prompts behind AI-made work, and hobbyists wanting hackable e-ink dashboards.

ideas.title: Prompt Receipts: shareable proof of how AI-made work was built
ideas.oneLiner: One-click bundle of the prompts, outputs and token usage behind an AI-assisted project, with a clean public page to link from a repo or post.
ideas.problem: Readers of AI-assisted projects and write-ups keep asking for the prompts, and authors have no standard way to share them along with results and cost. Prompts end up scattered across chat histories.
ideas.targetUsers: Developers and writers who publish AI-assisted code or articles and want credibility without a messy transcript dump.
ideas.monetization: Free for public receipts; ₹399/month for private receipts, custom domains and team libraries.
mvp: Import a Claude Code, Cursor or ChatGPT export into a normalized format
Redact secrets and pick which turns to publish
Shareable page with prompts, outputs and token/cost totals
Local prompt library with tags and search

competitors.name: GitHub Gists / pasted transcripts
competitors.gap: Unstructured; no token usage, redaction or consistent format.

competitors.name: Chat-export tools and AI session loggers
competitors.gap: Aimed at saving history for yourself rather than presenting a curated, shareable record; not verified in depth today.

sources.title: Comment on a thread about cloning apps with AI

sources.title: Comment on an AI-written project post
sources.quote: You should share the prompt or ask your agent to write a document other people’s agents can use to reimplement the code from scratch and/or customize to their specific needs.

sources.title: Comment on an AI-assisted write-up
sources.quote: Share your prompt or raw article notes even, it will much enjoyable to read than this

ideas.title: Panel: no-code layout builder for DIY e-ink dashboards
ideas.oneLiner: Design a home or desk dashboard in the browser and push it to any e-ink or ESP32 display as an image or JSON feed.
ideas.problem: Hobbyists want hackable e-ink displays for smart-home status, graphs and photos, but end up wiring an ESP32 and hand-coding every layout, with colour and large panels poorly served.
ideas.targetUsers: Makers and smart-home tinkerers with ESP32, TRMNL or InkPlate-style displays.
ideas.monetization: Free for 1 dashboard; ₹199/month for unlimited dashboards, hosted refresh endpoints and premium widgets.
mvp: Dithering and palette presets for B/W, 4-colour and full-colour panels
Hosted image endpoint with refresh schedule
Home Assistant and generic JSON/REST data sources

competitors.name: TRMNL
competitors.gap: Tied to its own hardware; a commenter still wants larger, tinker-friendly panels.

competitors.name: Home Assistant dashboards
competitors.gap: Built for LCD screens, not e-ink constraints; commenters prefer rolling their own ESP32 setups.

sources.title: Comment on a large e-ink panel thread
sources.quote: I wish there was a DIY company targeting hobbiests that sold large poster-size eInk panels with tinkering in mind, like TRMNL or InkPlate.
